items.subject: Petition under Section 79(1)(c) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 41 and 42 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the inter-state Transmission System) Regulations, 2022, inter alia seeking relaxation of Regulation 11A read with Regulation 5.8 (xi) pertaining to submission of documents demonstrating ownership of 50% of the land for return of Bank Guarantee submitted under Regulation 5.8(xi)(c). Indian Oil NTPC Green Energy Private Limited

Petition under Section 79(1)(c) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 41 and 42 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the inter-state Transmission System) Regulations, 2022, inter alia seeking relaxation of Regulation 11A read with Regulation 5.8 (xi) pertaining to submission of documents demonstrating ownership of 50% of the land for return of Bank Guarantee submitted under Regulation 5.8(xi)(c).

- _(d) Allow the Petitioner to use the land in its favour from NTPC Renewable Energy Limited and consequently direct CTUIL to accept such land documents._

- (f) _Pass such other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case_ .

**3.** The Petitioner has also sought the following interim reliefs vide main Petition:

- _(a) Grant ad-interim ex parte relief to the Petitioner restraining CTUIL from taking any coercive action against the Petitioner with respect to the 600 MW connectivity for Solar Project granted to the Petitioner at Bhuj PS, Gujarat, during pendency of the present Petition;_

- _(b) Direct CTUIL to not encash the Land BG of Rs. 60 cr. along with the ConnBG of Rs. 18.5 Cr. furnished by the Petitioner with respect to the 600 MW connectivity at Bhuj pooling station in Gujarat, during pendency of the present Petition;_

- _(e) Pass such other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case._

- _c) Pass any other order(s)/direction(s) as deemed necessary in the interest of justice and equity._

- **(i)** Further, in terms of Regulation 11B of the GNA Regulations, 2022, the Petitioner has to demonstrate ownership of 50% of the land within 18 months from the date of issuance of an in-principle grant of Connectivity or within 12 months of issuance of a final grant of Connectivity, whichever is earlier, which is 04.12.2025; otherwise, its connectivity shall be revoked and the Land BG of Rs. 60 cr. along with the Conn-BG of Rs. 18.5 Cr. shall be encashed by CTUIL. Hence, unless CTUIL accepts the land documents, which currently are in the name of NTPC REL, the Petitioner faces serious and irreparable prejudice, despite having substantially complied with the regulatory framework and completed land acquisition through an NTPC group entity.

- **(j)** The Petitioner is seeking the indulgence of this Commission to relax the requirement under Regulation 11A (1) read with Regulation 5.8(xi) for its project on the following grounds:

- **(iv)** The Petitioner is also in possession of 50% of the land for the Project, which has been allotted by the Government of Gujarat, which highlights its substantial compliance. However, the name mentioned in the allotment order is that of NTPC-REL. It is pertinent to note that the linkage detailed in the allotment order dated 09.11.2025 establishes that the ultimate

beneficiary of the land is the Petitioner; and NTPC-REL is merely an implementing entity.

_2. Learned counsel for the Respondent, CTUIL, submitted that apart from the issue raised by the Petitioner, it has also been observed that the land has been allotted for a solar power park, and a solar power park and a solar generator are distinct entities. Accordingly, this issue must also be addressed by the Petitioner._

_3. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the Parties, the Commission directed as under:_

- _(a) The Petitioner to implead NTPC Renewable Energy Ltd. (NTPC-REL) as a party to the Petition and file a revised memo of Parties within 2 days._

- _(c) The Respondents to file their reply before the next date of hearing with a copy to the Petitioner._

- _(d) The Petitioner to furnish the following information, on an affidavit, within two days, with a copy to the Respondent, who may, after examining the computation furnished by the Petitioner, file their comments, if any, before the next date of hearing:_

_(ii) Clarify why Petitioner granted No Objection Certificate (NOC) to the Govt. of Gujarat (GoG) to merge its application for land allotment with NTPC-REL application, and land NOCs obtained for its 600 MW project be considered for processing NTPC-REL’s application, even when the regulatory provision was clear then that the Petitioner itself has to satisfy conditions subsequent to the grant of connectivity._

**9.** During the hearing dated 03.12.2025, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that Petitioner, vide letter dated 26.11.2025, has again approached GPCL/Govt. of Gujarat for resolution of land document issues, requesting to allow the execution of the lease agreement directly in the name of the Petitioner (instead of NTPCREL) and for issuance of NOC for development of its Solar Project in the land allotted for the Solar Park, and further, the Petitioner is also meeting with the concerned authorities in this regard. Learned counsel also prayed for a direction to maintain the status quo till the next date of hearing.

**10.** Considering the facts & circumstances and submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties, the Commission directed the parties to maintain the status quo till the next date of hearing.

_3. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels for the Petitioner and the Respondents, the Commission directed the parties to maintain the status quo till the outcome of the Petition._

_4. Based on the request of the parties, the Commission permitted the parties to file their respective written submissions/ Note of arguments within two weeks with a copy to other side._

- **c)** In case Land documents submitted by the Petitioner are not found in Order by the CTUIL or if the Petitioner fails to furnish the compensation charges within the stipulated time, CTUIL shall proceed with action in terms of the GNA Regulations.

2. PGCIL has submitted that the Commission in its order dated 31.3.2021 in Petition No.104/TT/2020 approved the COD of four number 220 kV bays at Dehradun sub-station (i.e. Asset-III in the said petition) as 4.2.2017 in terms of the second proviso to clause 3 of Regulation 4 of the 2014 Tariff Regulations, as the associated downstream assets under the scope of PTCUL, was not constructed by it. It has also submitted that the Commission in the said order held that the transmission charges of Asset-III shall be borne by PTCUL from its COD (4.2.2017) till the COD of the downstream assets under the scope of PTCUL. The relevant portion of the order dated 31.3.2021 is extracted below:

3. PGCIL has submitted that it has raised invoices on PTCUL in accordance with the

order dated 31.3.2021 in Petition No.104/TT/2021, but PTUCL has failed to pay the

transmission charges as directed by the Commission in the said order. Accordingly, PGCIL filed the present petition seeking enforcement/ execution of the Commission’s order dated 31.3.2021, directing bilateral billing and payment of transmission charges by PTCUL to PGCIL, on account of delay in the commissioning of downstream transmission network by PTCUL. PGCIL also submitted that PTCUL has filed Appeal No. 410/2022 challenging the Commission’s order dated 31.3.2021 in Petition No. 104/TT/2020 before the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) and since there is no interim order of stay against the Commission’s order, the present petition has been filed subject to the outcome of the pending appeal.

4. During the pendency of this petition, APTEL, vide its judgement dated 2.7.2026, disposed of Appeal No.410/2022, holding as under:

_“62. Therefore, it directly flows from (iii) above in paragraph 58 that the liability of transmission charges for four unutilised bays cannot be fastened on PTCUL. The question as to whether PTCUL could have been saddled with liability of transmission charges had a contractual arrangement been found to exist on the basis of the MoM when Regulations provide for recovery through pool, is purely academic in the present proceedings. Accordingly, it is neither necessary nor appropriate to express any opinion on that question. xxx”_

_For the foregoing reasons as stated above, we are of the considered view that the captioned Appeal No. 410 of 2022 has merit and is allowed._

_However, since the question as to who should bear the transmission charges in respect of the four unutilized bays during the period they remained unused survives for consideration, the matter is remanded to the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission for fresh adjudication limited to the said issue, in accordance with law and in the light of the observations contained in this Judgment._

_While undertaking the_ _<u>remand exercise, the Central Commission shall be at liberty to</u> examine all relevant facts and circumstances, including but not limited to the issues identified in paragraph 106 of this Judgment, and any other factors that may have a bearing on determination of the appropriate mechanism for recovery of transmission charges relating to the said bays._

_The Captioned Appeal and pending IAs, if any, are disposed of in the above terms.”_

matter (Petition No. 104/TT/2020) to the Commission for reconsideration on the limited issue as to who should bear the transmission charges in respect of the four unutilized bays at Dehradun substation.

6. During the hearing of the present Petition along with Petition No.104/TT/2020 (on remand) on 11.11.2026, the learned counsel for PTCUL referred to paragraph 62 of the judgement dated 2.7.2026 and submitted that since APTEL has clearly held that PTCUL cannot be held liable for payment of the transmission charges in respect of the four bays at Dehradun substation, the present Petition seeking execution of the order dated 31.3.2021 in Petition No. 104/TT/2020 against PTCUL, does not survive for consideration and hence the same may be disposed of. The learned counsel for PGCIL also submitted that the present Petition may be disposed of and the filing fees deposited by PGCIL may be adjusted.

7. We have considered the submissions of the parties. Considering the fact that APTEL vide its judgement dated 2.7.2026 in Appeal No.410/2022, has held that PTCUL cannot be held liable for payment of the transmission charges in respect of the four bays at Dehradun Substation to PGCIL, the present Petition filed by PGCIL for execution of the order dated 31.3.2021 in Petition No.104/TT/2020 against PTCUL has been rendered infructuous and the same deserves to be disposed of.  Accordingly, the present Petition is disposed of as infructuous. Further, PGCIL’s prayer for adjustment of the filing fees paid in this petition is allowed, and the same shall be adjusted against the petitions to be filed in future by PGCIL.
